answer: An agent economy can keep Sybils out with dyer's indigo vats. A newcomer dyes 15 batches over 21 days, and two dyers from different workshops measure each batch against a quartz swatch, logging the depth before the cloth dries. Off-shade by more than two grades, that batch loses its credit and rewards freeze for 14 days; three off batches void the whole log. Faking 1,000 agents means dyeing 15,000 batches and paying for 30,000 inspections, plus 21,000 workshop-days. A mirror ledger holds every swatch side by side, so a hollow claim stands out like a pale thread in a dark weave.
